nodes.summary: The Fitting subgroup `F(G)`: the join of the nilpotent normal subgroups of `G` (for finite `G` the largest nilpotent normal subgroup).
nodes.title: Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of a group $G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such intersections, that is, that contain no other intersection of this form.
nodes.title: Subgroup generated by the inclusion-minimal triple intersections

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such intersections is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Inclusion-minimal triple intersections need not lie in the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such intersections is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Inclusion-minimal triple intersections and the Fitting subgroup (Kourovka 20.122(b), (c))

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a nilpotent injector when, for every subnormal subgroup $K$ of $G$, the intersection $H \cap K$ is nilpotent and is a maximal nilpotent subgroup of $K$: every nilpotent subgroup $L$ of $G$ with $H \cap K \le L \le K$ equals $H \cap K$.
nodes.title: Nilpotent injector

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of a group $G$, the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) whose order is at most the order of every such intersection.
nodes.title: Subgroup generated by the triple intersections of least order

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ generated by the intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) of least order is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Minimal-order triple intersections need not lie in the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ generated by the intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) of least order is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Minimal-order triple intersections and the Fitting subgroup (Kourovka 20.122(a), (c))

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $k$ such that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, \dots, g_k \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap \dots \cap g_k H g_k^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Boundedly many conjugates of a nilpotent injector meet in the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: The assertion that there is a natural number $k$ such that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, \dots, g_k \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap \dots \cap g_k H g_k^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.37(a)

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, g_2, g_3 \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap g_2 H g_2^{-1} \cap g_3 H g_3^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Three conjugates of a nilpotent injector meet in the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: The assertion that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, g_2, g_3 \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap g_2 H g_2^{-1} \cap g_3 H g_3^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.37(b)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian simple group and let $A$ and $B$ be nilpotent subgroups of $G$. Then there is $x \in G$ with $A \cap x B x^{-1} = 1$.
nodes.title: Nilpotent subgroups of a finite simple group have conjugates meeting trivially

nodes.summary: The assertion, in the two-subgroup form of its resolution, that for every finite non-abelian simple group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$ with $A \cap x B x^{-1} = 1$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 15.40

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$ there are $x, y \in G$ with $N \cap x N x^{-1} \cap y N y^{-1} \le F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Three conjugates of a nilpotent subgroup meet inside the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: The assertion that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$ there are $x, y \in G$ with $N \cap x N x^{-1} \cap y N y^{-1} \le F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.40

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of a group $G$, this is the set of all subgroups of $G$ of the form $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$, that is, the intersections of $A$ with a conjugate of $B$ and a conjugate of $C$.
nodes.title: Triple intersections with conjugates

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
